title: BHU Campus, Varanasi - A Green, Grand & Historic World Within a City
content:
BHU Campus, Varanasi

The Banaras Hindu University (BHU) campus is one of the largest and most beautiful residential universities in Asia.
Spread across 1,300+ acres, the campus is a perfect blend of historic architecture, peaceful greenery, grand temples, museums, and academic excellence.
Visitors often call BHU “a city inside a city” because of its wide roads, gardens, hostels, libraries, and vibrant student life.

History & Significance

Founded in 1916 by freedom fighter Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, BHU was built to combine traditional Indian values with modern education.
The campus has played a major role in India’s cultural, educational, and social development.
Its iconic buildings, calm environment, and spiritual atmosphere make it a must-visit place in Varanasi.

BHU is home to more than 30,000 students from across India and the world, making it a symbol of knowledge, unity, and diversity.

What to See Inside BHU Campus

1. New Vishwanath Temple (Birla Mandir): The most famous attraction inside BHU. A tall, stunning white temple inspired by the original Kashi Vishwanath Temple, offering a peaceful environment for meditation.

2. Bharat Kala Bhavan Museum: A treasure house of Indian arts, sculptures, textiles, paintings, and archaeological collections. It is one of India’s finest university museums.

3. Lush Green Avenues & Gardens: Wide tree-lined roads, botanical gardens, and open spaces make the campus perfect for walking, cycling, and photography.

4. Central Library: One of the largest university libraries in India with lakhs of books, ancient manuscripts, and modern digital facilities.

5. Amphitheatre & Faculty Buildings: Beautiful structures reflecting Indo-Gothic and modern architecture, showcasing the heritage of BHU.

6. Student Life & Cultural Events: The campus buzzes with festivals, seminars, sports events, and vibrant student activities throughout the year.

Best Time to Visit

  • Morning & Evening - cool weather and beautiful light
  • Winter months - perfect for walking and exploring
  • Avoid visiting during peak summer afternoons

Nearby Places to Visit

  • Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
  • Durga Kund Temple
  • Tulsi Manas Temple
  •  Assi Ghat
  • Tulsi Ghat

faqs.question: Why is BHU famous?
faqs.answer: For its large campus, quality education, Vishwanath Temple, and rich heritage.

faqs.question: Can visitors explore the campus?
faqs.answer: Yes, the campus is open to visitors during the day.

faqs.question: What is the main attraction inside BHU?
faqs.answer: The New Vishwanath Temple and Bharat Kala Bhavan Museum.

faqs.question: How much time is needed to explore BHU?
faqs.answer: 1-2 hours is enough for a comfortable visit.

faqs.question: Is photography allowed?
faqs.answer: Yes, photography is allowed on the campus except inside certain buildings.
